findings.problem: The repair's new 7-over-8 discriminator rests on a gap the article's most-cited source contradicts, and leaves out a circumstance its own evidence record names. Patel's 2024 account (S01) says "In 2022, I also started going to every conference I could." Substrate (S08), which the article cites 53 times, says "By 2021, Dylan's itinerary had become a succession of acronyms: ISSCC, DAC, ECTC," and places the early travel "As the pandemic progressed". The body still says "two years before the conferences" and "from 2022 it explains much of the travel". The Why-not-8 FAQ says he hit the road "two years before conferences gave him a business reason to travel". The type section offers the 2020 move as his "clearest dated example" of a Seven's fear of being boxed in. The article never mentions the pandemic, yet C139's alternative says the 2020-2021 travel "overlapped a pandemic in which conferences were limited". That is a non-temperament explanation for the very gap the article says tips the read. C41, C137, C138 and C139 cite only S01 and do not record S08's 2021 dating. This argument was written in repair, after the six-role jury reviewed the draft. It is now the deciding Seven evidence, and no reviewer has challenged it.
findings.acceptance_test: Body, type section and Why-not-8 FAQ stop stating the two-year gap as fact. They either attribute the 2022 start to Patel's 2024 account and note Substrate's 2021 dating, or drop the gap length. The discriminator paragraph tells the reader the 2020 move came during the pandemic, with a quiet-quit paycheck. C41, C137, C138 and C139 record S08's "By 2021" passage and the pandemic. The article then either shows, with sourced specifics, why the timing still separates Seven from Eight, or says the 7/8 call cannot be tipped on the current record. Because the deciding argument has been rewritten twice since the frozen jury review, release requires `--refresh --expanded-review` (or a research-stage hold if no discriminator survives), not another blind repair.
